Translate business priorities into clear technology initiatives, features, milestones, and delivery plans. Manage overall delivery timelines, dependencies, scope, risks, issues, and priorities. Facilitate alignment across business and technology stakeholders and ensure timely decisions. Track delivery progress and proactively identify issues that may impact scope, schedule, quality, or business outcomes. Establish and maintain an effective delivery cadence, including status meetings, planning sessions, risk reviews, and stakeholder communications. Coordinate multiple teams and workstreams to ensure initiatives move forward in a structured and predictable manner. Help business and technology teams identify process impacts, dependencies, and opportunities for improvement. Ensure that functional requirements and business priorities are sufficiently clear for the technical team to estimate and deliver. Technical Coordination Work closely with the Technical Product Owner without assuming technical ownership. Coordinate technical dependencies across applications and delivery teams. Ensure technical risks, constraints, and decisions are communicated effectively to business stakeholders. Facilitate discussions between business and technical teams when requirements, priorities, or solution options need clarification. Support resolution of cross-team issues and escalate decisions when required. Coordinate testing, UAT, deployment, cutover, and go-live activities from a product and delivery perspective. Stakeholder Management Build strong working relationships with Business Product Owners, Technical Product Owners, business SMEs, architects, developers, QA teams, vendors, and IT leadership. Create transparency between business and technology regarding priorities, timelines, risks, dependencies, and delivery status. Facilitate communication between stakeholders with different business and technical perspectives. Drive accountability for actions, decisions, and deliverables across participating teams. Prepare clear and concise executive-level status reporting and product updates. Required Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Supply Chain, Computer Science, or a related discipline. 7+ years of experience in IT product management, IT project management, technology delivery, or a related role. Strong experience managing scope, priorities, timelines, dependencies, risks, issues, and stakeholder expectations. Strong functional understanding of Supply Chain, Distribution, Warehouse Management, and Order-to-Cash processes. Experience working with WMS, ERP, OMS, TMS, or related Supply Chain applications. Demonstrated ability to operate between business and technology teams and translate business needs into actionable technology requirements. Strong communication, facilitation, prioritization, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills. Ability to understand technical concepts without being the technical solution owner. Preferred Experience Experience with WMS platforms such as Manhattan, Blue Yonder, SAP EWM, Oracle WMS, or similar. Experience in retail, wholesale, manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or eCommerce environments. Experience working in Agile, Scrum, or hybrid product delivery environments. Experience managing products or platforms with multiple upstream and downstream system dependencies. Experience working with third-party technology vendors and implementation partners. PMP, Product Management, Scrum, or Agile certification is a plus. The IT Product Manager is primarily accountable for: Business-to-technology alignment Product and delivery coordination Prioritization and planning Scope, timeline, risk, and dependency management Stakeholder communication Business outcome alignment Coordinating Business Product Owner and Technical Product Owner activities Ensuring successful delivery of product capabilities The role should be able to understand technology without being the technology owner and understand the business process deeply enough to ensure that technology delivery solves the right business problem. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate is a strong IT Product Manager who understands Supply Chain. They can engage confidently with business leaders and Product Owners while also working effectively with technical teams. They understand the end-to-end Order-to-Cash journey, have practical knowledge of distribution and warehouse operations, and can connect business priorities to technology delivery. They are highly organized, proactive in managing risks and dependencies, comfortable driving cross-functional teams, and skilled at bringing business and technical stakeholders together to make decisions and deliver outcomes.
